subject: paper:barkley-1997
quote: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) comprises a deficit in behavioral inhibition. A theoretical model is constructed that links inhibition to 4 executive neuropsychological functions that appear to depend on it for their effective execution: (a) working memory, (b) self-regulation of affect-motivation-arousal, (c) internalization of speech, and (d) reconstitution (behavioral analysis and synthesis).
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The foundational statement of the inhibition-centred executive-function theory of ADHD.

subject: paper:willcutt-2005-ef-meta
quote: Groups with ADHD exhibited significant impairment on all EF tasks. Effect sizes for all measures fell in the medium range (.46-.69), but the strongest and most consistent effects were obtained on measures of response inhibition, vigilance, working memory, and planning.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Meta-analysis of 83 studies establishing which EF domains are impaired in ADHD and at what magnitude — the empirical content of the mechanism.

subject: paper:willcutt-2005-ef-meta
quote: However, moderate effect sizes and lack of universality of EF deficits among individuals with ADHD suggest that EF weaknesses are neither necessary nor sufficient to cause all cases of ADHD.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The crucial nuance against a single-EF-deficit account, and the empirical basis for the core-vs-one-component tension.

subject: paper:barkley-fischer-2011
quote: We conclude that EF ratings are better predictors of impairment in major life activities generally and occupational functioning specifically at adult follow-up than are EF tests.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Real-world EF ratings out-predict lab EF tests for adult impairment — extending the rating-vs-task dissociation into the ecological-validity domain.

subject: paper:toplak-2013
quote: Only 68 (24%) of the 286 relevant correlations reported in these studies were statistically significant, and the overall median correlation was only .19.
rationale: Verbatim (verified against author-hosted full text; reused from the measurement note). Rating-based and task-based EF measures barely converge — method variance dominates, so a lab EF test and a real-world EF report are not interchangeable.
